note:
WHICH BRAIDS PARAMETER DRIVES WHAT, WITH LINE NUMBERS (braids/digital_oscillator.cc). TIMBRE is parameter_[0] and is the modulation INDEX in all three shapes: :728/:731 open BEGIN_INTERPOLATE_PARAMETER_0, and parameter_0 scales the modulator at :740 (FM, `<< 2` = a full cycle of deviation), :777/:780 (FBFM, `<< 1` = half) and :811 (WTFM, `<< 1`). COLOR is parameter_[1] and is the modulator RATIO: Render() quantizes it through lut_fm_frequency_quantizer at :99-107 before dispatch, and it is then added to the modulator's pitch at :726 (FM), :762 (FBFM) and :796 (WTFM). In FBFM it feeds one more thing -- the index attenuator at :756-759 -- which is why this file sweeps note and ratio together in that shape. So p1 -> the engine's TIMBRE and p2 -> its HARMONICS.

MORPH IS NOT A SPARE MACRO HERE: it is the shape selector, and its three A/B positions are exactly the three Braids models. raw_fm_engine.cc gives phase_feedback = 1 / frequency_feedback = 0 at MORPH 0 (FEEDBACK_FM), both zero at MORPH 0.5 (plain FM), and phase_feedback = 0 / frequency_feedback = 1 at MORPH 1 (CHAOTIC_FEEDBACK_FM). Every case pins MORPH to 0.0, 0.5 or 1.0 to match its own `shape`. MACRO is the one axis the port adds beyond Braids: feedback depth, ApplyMacro(1.0, 0.0, 1.5, macro), which returns Braids' own depth of 1.0 at the 0.5 detent. It sits at 0.5 in every case but `fm-macro-min` and `fm-macro-max`, which drive it to both ends at MORPH 0.5 -- where depth multiplies two terms that are already zero -- to prove it is inert there. Both read 0.04 dB, identical to `fm-stock`.

HARMONICS IS NOT SET EQUAL TO p2, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Braids quantizes COLOR through its OWN lut_fm_frequency_quantizer (129 entries, 25 plateaus of 3+ equal entries, spanning -36..+36 semitones); the port reads PLAITS' table of the same name (130 entries, 23 plateaus, spanning -12..+36) -- Braids' table with the -36 and -24 plateaus removed and the ramps between the survivors resampled about twice as finely. Same idea, different plateau positions, so equal knob angles are different ratios: p2 = 0.5 is +6 semitones on the module while HARMONICS = 0.5 is +12.16 in the port. Comparing knob angle to knob angle would measure only that remap and would hide every other defect behind it. Each case instead pins the two sides to the SAME modulator ratio, read off the two tables (each pair verified to agree to 0.00000 semitones by evaluating both quantizers):

    ratio      Braids p2   port HARMONICS
    -12 st     0.2815      0.0078
      0 st     0.4299      0.2344
    +12 st     0.5940      0.4766
    +24 st     0.8282      0.7500
    +36 st     0.9883      0.9883

The exception is `ratio-floor-knob-parity`, the only case that sets both sides to their own axis MINIMUM, because that is the one place the remap is not a relabelling: Braids reaches -36 semitones and the port's table bottoms out at -12, so the module's bottom two ratio plateaus are unreachable. It carries no tolerance -- it documents the table-span difference rather than gating on it.

The note is 45 (A2) unless a case says otherwise, low enough that neither side's aliasing dominates the spectral figure.

STATE: ALL 25 TOLERANCED CASES PASS. The three that used to fail were the two findings recorded below, both now fixed in the engine; a third quantisation defect that no case was gating on was fixed with them. Nothing in this file was widened, removed or weakened to get there -- the three tolerances the fixes had to clear (1.0 dB AC RMS / 1.5 dB spectrum on `fbfm-index-attenuator`, `fbfm-attenuator-note84` and `fm-modulator-clamp`) are the house numbers and are unchanged from the failing revision. Two cases were ADDED afterwards, in review, to close a hole the fixes left in this file -- see COVERAGE ADDED IN REVIEW below.

TOLERANCES, AND WHY ANY OF THEM IS LOOSE. Twenty-five of the twenty-nine cases carry a tolerance. Twenty of those carry the house numbers unchanged -- 1.0 dB AC RMS, 1.5 dB spectrum, and 1 cent where cents is measured at all -- and all twenty pass, most by a wide margin (fm-stock 0.04 dB, wtfm-note72 0.03 dB, wtfm-index-max 0.06 dB). Five cases deviate from the house numbers, each for a stated reason:

* The three index-0 cases carry `cents: 2.0`. All three render the bare carrier (index 0 collapses all three shapes to the same sine) and all three report the same +1.7 cents, while their spectra agree to 0.05 dB. A 65536-point windowed-FFT peak on the same two WAVs puts the real difference at -0.29 cents after the kCorrectedSampleRate offset, so the +1.7 is ab_compare's autocorrelation estimator biased on a single sinusoid, not a pitch error.
* `fbfm-index-max` carries `acRmsDb: 1.5` and `spectrumDb: 2.0`, and reads +1.31 dB / 1.88 dB. Measured in narrow bands, the port matches the reference to within 1.2 dB everywhere below 15 kHz and is +5.9, +20.0 and +39.9 dB in 15-21k, 21-23k and 23-24k. That is the one-sample feedback loop running at 48 kHz: its near-Nyquist limit cycle lands at ~24 kHz, where Braids' identical loop at 96 kHz puts it at ~48 kHz and the reference decimator removes it. It is the declared no-oversampling deviation, confined to the top octave, and it is what the +1.31 dB of AC RMS is made of. This case is at note 45 with a 1:1 ratio, i.e. 27 semitones BELOW the FBFM attenuator's pivot, so the attenuator fix does not touch it and its numbers are unchanged.
* `fm-aliasing-note80` carries `spectrumDb: 2.0` and reads 1.33. This is the same no-oversampling deviation in PLAIN FM, which the FBFM case above does not cover: at note 80 with a +36 st ratio the modulator is 6.6 kHz and half a cycle of deviation throws sidebands past 27 kHz, so 14.6% of the port's energy lands in 20.5-24 kHz where Braids at 96 kHz has none. `fm-modulator-clamp-control` is the control -- same note region, +12 st, sidebands under Nyquist, 0.20 dB.
* Cents is omitted, not widened, wherever the f0 estimator is unreliable: the four CHAOTIC_FEEDBACK_FM cases at non-zero index (chaotic frequency feedback, inharmonic by construction) and every deep-index or wide-ratio case at note 72 or above, where autocorrelation locks onto a sub-octave or super-octave lag. `fm-attenuator-control` is the proof: it reports +1200.0 cents while its spectrum agrees to 0.10 dB. Do not read the cents column on any of those cases as evidence in either direction -- see FIX 1.

FIX 1 (LANDED): THE FBFM INDEX ATTENUATOR. Braids' RenderFeedbackFm scales the modulation index by a pitch- and ratio-dependent ramp (digital_oscillator.cc:756-759, applied at :777): attenuation = clip(32767 - 4 * (pitch_ - 72*128 + ratio_offset), 0, 32767), then p = parameter_0 * attenuation >> 15. pitch_ and ratio_offset are in 1/128 semitone, so the slope is 4*128 = 512 parts of 32768 -- unity at or below note 72 with a ratio at or under 1:1, falling 1.5625% of the index per semitone of MODULATOR pitch above that, and zero 64 semitones up. The port had no equivalent term; its index depended only on TIMBRE and MORPH. raw_fm_engine.cc now computes the same ramp in float and rides it in on `phase_feedback`, so it is full at MORPH 0, gone by noon and absent in the chaotic half -- exactly the three Braids models. Plaits' own `two-op-fm`, the direct descendant of this code, keeps the same device with the same note-72 pivot (fm_engine.cc:84-87, squared rather than linear).

  EVIDENCE, BEFORE -> AFTER. `fbfm-index-attenuator` (note 72, +24 st, index 1; attenuator 0.625) 5.81 dB -> 1.01 dB. The four bands that carry the sound went +1.70 -> +0.13 dB (7.7% of energy), +2.79 -> +0.11 (15.2%), +6.39 -> -0.08 (36.0%) and +15.37 -> +2.77 (14.3%). `fbfm-attenuator-note84` (note 84, 1:1; attenuator 0.8125) 2.50 dB -> 0.94 dB. `fbfm-ratio-ceiling` (note 45, +36 st; attenuator 0.859) was inside tolerance already and still improved, 1.13 dB -> 0.56 dB. `fm-attenuator-control` -- plain FM at the same note and ratio, where Braids has no attenuator either -- was 0.10 dB and is 0.10 dB, i.e. the ramp did not leak into the wrong shape. `fbfm-stock`, `fbfm-index-min`, `fbfm-index-max` and `fbfm-ratio-floor` all sit below the pivot and are unchanged to the last digit.

  `fbfm-attenuator-emulated` HAS FLIPPED MEANING and is kept for that reason. It renders the same reference with the port's TIMBRE hand-set to 0.625, Braids' attenuation factor at note 72. While the ramp was missing that emulated it and the case came good at 1.01 dB; now the engine applies its own 0.625 on top, the effective index is 0.39, and the case reads 4.96 dB with every energy-bearing band 1.2 to 10.1 dB LOW. It carries no tolerance and is not an A/B -- it is the double-attenuation signature, and it going quiet again would mean the ramp had been dropped.

  WHAT IS NOT EVIDENCE, because it is easy to reach for and it is wrong. (a) The sub-160 Hz bands still read -35 to +8 dB on these cases, but they carry 0.0% of the energy on both sides; that is a ratio of two noise floors, and the two cases disagree in sign. (b) The cents column reads -1199.6 on `fbfm-index-attenuator` even now that it passes at 1.01 dB. The octave is the estimator, not a defect.

FIX 2 (LANDED): BRAIDS' MODULATOR PITCH CEILING. All three shapes build the modulator increment as ComputePhaseIncrement((12 << 7) + pitch_ + ratio_offset) >> 1 (:726, :762, :796), and ComputePhaseIncrement pins its argument at kPitchTableStart - 1 = (128 << 7) - 1 (:51-54). The `>> 1` is an exact octave down, so the module's modulator saturates at 128 - 1/128 - 12 = 115.9921875 semitones, 6641.9 Hz, however much further the ratio knob turns. The port instead capped the modulator at Nyquist (min(frequency * SemitonesToRatio(ratio), 0.5f)), nearly four octaves higher, so above note 80 at the top of the ratio axis the two engines were running different modulators. raw_fm_engine.cc now clamps the modulator NOTE at 115.9921875 and keeps the Nyquist min behind it as a guard for hosts below 13.3 kHz.

  EVIDENCE, BEFORE -> AFTER. `fm-modulator-clamp` (note 96, +36 st) 4.24 dB -> 0.68 dB. `fm-modulator-clamp-emulated` renders the same reference with the port's HARMONICS hand-set to 0.681297 = +19.99 st, the ratio Braids' clamp actually delivers at note 96; the clamped engine and that hand-picked ratio now produce the SAME numbers in every band and the same 0.68 dB overall, which is the tightest available statement that the clamp lands where Braids' does. The 0.68 dB that remains is the no-oversampling deviation, +0.56 dB in 20.5-24 kHz on 14.9% of the energy. `fm-modulator-clamp-control` (note 96, +12 st, below the ceiling) was 0.20 dB and is 0.20 dB.

  SCOPE. The clamp engages when carrier note + ratio reaches 115.9921875: from note 80 at the top of the ratio axis, note 92 at +24 st, note 104 at +12 st, and -- contrary to what the pre-fix version of this note claimed -- from note 116 at 1:1, since voice.cc clamps p.note at 120, so the top four semitones of the note range reach it with the ratio knob at centre. `fm-aliasing-note80` is exactly one 1/128 semitone into it -- a 4 Hz trim on a 6.65 kHz modulator -- which is why that case moved slightly, 1.47 dB -> 1.33 dB, without changing what it measures. The ceiling is now named in the engine header, the README and plaits-engine.json's HARMONICS description.

COVERAGE ADDED IN REVIEW. Two cases were added after the fixes landed, because between them the fixes created a region no case reached. `fbfm-clamp-and-attenuator` is the important one: FEEDBACK_FM at note 96 with a +36 st ratio is the only place where the FIX 1 ramp and the FIX 2 ceiling are BOTH engaged, and the two read the ratio differently on purpose -- the modulator is pinned at 115.99 st while the attenuator ramp reads the UNCLAMPED 132 st and lands on 2047/32768 = 0.0625, which is what Braids does (the ramp at :756-759 is computed from parameter_[1] directly and never sees ComputePhaseIncrement's pin at :52-53). Nothing in the shipped 27 cases could tell that apart from the obvious alternative: rewriting the ramp to read the clamped modulator note gives 0.3126 instead, a 5x index error, and it passes every one of the 27. It fails this case at 4.24 dB, and the pre-fix engine fails it at 7.73 dB, against 0.16 dB as shipped. `fbfm-attenuator-zero` is the far end of the same ramp -- note 108 at +36 st is 72 semitones past the pivot, so Braids' clip pins the index at zero -- and it carries NO tolerance because it cannot gate anything: when the reference is a bare sine, its whole spectrum sits in one band, every band the port adds sidebands to has ~0% of the reference's energy and so ~0 weight, and match_level absorbs what is left. Measured proof that the case is toothless rather than merely quiet: the PRE-FIX engine, which has no attenuator at all and modulates at 0.5 cycles where the module modulates at zero, reads 1.14 dB here -- inside the house 1.5. It is kept as a documented blind spot, not as coverage.

FIX 3 (LANDED, NO CASE WAS GATING ON IT): WTFM'S FREQUENCY FEEDBACK IS A STAIRCASE. Braids reads the feedback as modulator_phase += (modulator_phase_increment >> 8) * (129 + (previous_sample >> 9)) (:814-815). `>> 9` on a signed int16 is an arithmetic shift, i.e. a FLOOR, so the multiplier moves in 128 steps of 1/256 between 65/256 and 192/256, with a downward bias of up to one step -- not the continuous ramp the port was computing. previous_sample * 32768 >> 9 is floor(previous_sample * 64) once the sample is a float in [-1, 1], and the port now floors it that way, clipped to the int16-reachable -64..+63.

  EVIDENCE. No case was failing on this, so the numbers are small and they are all in the right direction: `wtfm-stock` 0.07 -> 0.06 dB, `wtfm-index-max` 0.09 -> 0.06 dB, `wtfm-ratio-ceiling` 0.10 -> 0.14 dB, `wtfm-index-min` and `wtfm-note72` unchanged. The reason to make the change anyway is that WTFM is chaotic: a spectral average over two seconds cannot distinguish a trajectory that tracks the module's from one that merely has the same statistics, so the arithmetic has to be right rather than the summary statistic.

  NOT REPRODUCED, and deliberately: the companion `modulator_phase_increment >> 8` floors the increment onto multiples of 256 in the module's 2^32 phase accumulator at 96 kHz. That floor is a function of the module's sample rate, so it has no rate-independent form to port into a 48 kHz engine; at the modulator frequencies this engine reaches it is a downward bias under 0.05 cents.

RESIDUALS, AND THE ONE THAT IS NOT ABOVE 10 kHz. Most of what is left is the declared no-oversampling deviation showing up as a top-octave EXCESS: `fbfm-index-max` +1.31 dB AC RMS (its ~24 kHz limit cycle), `fbfm-index-attenuator` +2.77 dB in 10-20k and +18.33 dB in 20.5-24k on 14.3% and 2.4% of the energy, `fbfm-attenuator-note84` +1.95 and +13.74 dB on 14.2% and 3.1%, `fm-aliasing-note80` +3.27 dB in 20.5-24k on 14.6%. `fbfm-stock` is the exception and should not be filed with them: at 1.06 dB it is the third-largest toleranced residual, none of it is above 10 kHz, and its sign is the other way -- the port reads -0.98 dB at 1.3-2.6k (13.1% of the energy), -2.30 at 2.6-5.1k (10.3%) and -4.80 at 5.1-10k (6.2%), i.e. it is DARKER than the module, not brighter. That is the other face of running the feedback loop at 48 kHz rather than 96: the module's loop generates harmonics up to 48 kHz and its decimator keeps everything under 24 kHz, while this loop simply never makes them. It is unchanged by all three fixes (measured 1.06 dB before and after) and it is the largest audible-band divergence in the file. `ratio-floor-knob-parity` reads 6.75 dB and carries no tolerance by design -- it is the -36 vs -12 ratio-table span, a Plaits-side table difference, not a port defect.
